Aug. 16Trump had a 35% approval rating and 55% disapproval rating in a Financial Times/Focaldata poll of 1,913 registered voters conducted Aug. 7-10 (margin of error 2.9).

Trump’s net approval rating among Republicans has dropped eight points since the groups’ survey last month, the Financial Times reported.

The poll comes as inflation cooled in July from June, but at 3.4%, it’s still higher than when Trump took office as the war with Iran has driven up fuel costs and disrupted the economy. ### Similar survey findings

A New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Sienna poll released this week surveyed 760 Pennsylvania voters and found similar sentiments heading into November.

Fifty-one percent of that poll’s respondents said they would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate if the election took place today, compared with 44% of people who favored Republicans. Trump’s approval ratings were also low, with 58% of people saying they disapprove of his work. results.content: Recent surveys have indicated that Democrats are leading over Republicans on generic ballots, with just a few months before the pivotal November midterm elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll released this week found that 42% of registered voters said they would cast their ballot for a Democratic congressional candidate if the midterms were held that day, while 37% would back a Republican congressional candidate.
